briefhow.text: Briefing mode follows the story-mode pattern: map + slide card + a bottom strip. DAILY (real 12 Sep edition): THE DAY (headline + summary + stats) → 8 TOP STORIES (map flies to their countries; each AI forecast labelled model judgment, later scored on Track record) → COUNTRY TO WATCH (opens the country card) + rising thread. EDITIONS strip: solid = published (5–12 Sep), dashed = no edition (13–25 Sep, AI paused) — never a dead end. WEEKLY (week of 6 Sep): THE WEEK → 6 SIGNALS (fact, then our "so what") → NEXT WEEK watch list. READ AS TEXT keeps a plain version for email/print/search.

cTitle.text: C · Country (card on the map; deep-dive in the Studio)

cardhow.text: Clicking an event on the home page opens its story card in the right-hand column. The map stays and turns to the story. Order: WHAT IS HAPPENING (summary) → WHAT IT MEANS (bottom line + most likely path) → WHY (a 2–3 step cause chain, fact ✅ / inference 💭). Links inside the summary: a dotted underline = an event in this story (opens the full story at the timeline); a coloured-dot link = another story we track (opens that story card here, with ← BACK TO …). Every block has its own link into the matching section of the full story; OPEN FULL STORY sits at the bottom. Try: click the Leipzig drone link in the AfD card, then BACK. Hover the Leipzig link first to see its StoryPeek.

countryhow.text: Country card — v2 after a two-critic debate. Five real states: IRAN briefed but 14 days old (amber) — score at the TOP OF THE SCALE so no arrow; latest axis move shown instead. GERMANY — NOT ENOUGH READINGS (no data 22 Aug–4 Sep), so no trend claimed. YEMEN — last briefed 18 Aug, too old to show; shows story count + where it is mentioned in the Iran briefing. BRAZIL — never briefed; stories + figures + Generate in Studio. URUGUAY — no coverage: a small popover, never implying "safe". One screen, no scroll: risk bars open their WHY on click; facts only when verified; dated forecast triggers only, never passed ones.

peekhow.text: ONE shared piece, reused everywhere a story is mentioned: hover (or keyboard-focus) any story link, map pin or web bubble and this StoryPeek appears — type, status, headline, one-line brief, counts + honest updated-time, and what a click will do. Try it: the Leipzig link in the home card (row 3, below), the globe/radar pins (row 2), and the board MAP and WEB views. All of those screens import this one file; change it here and they all change. Phones have no hover: a tap goes straight to the card, which is the preview.

srhow.text: E2 is the one-screen, game-style alternative to E1 (the scroll page). References: Return of the Obra Dinn’s book of fates (a grid where every case stays visible and fills in only when confirmed) = the FORECAST BOARD; a roguelike seed = THIS WEEK’S DRAW, published in advance; GitHub’s contribution graph / a training log = the SETTLING LOG (one square per week — the empty weeks after the July pilot are shown in red, not hidden); chess.com Game Review = ACCURACY, always beside a plain guess and locked until enough questions resolve; the Paradox “ledger” = WHEN WE CHANGED OUR READ. Click tiles, weeks and ledger entries; switch stages at the top. E1 can remain as the plain-text version. NEW: BOARD | MAP switch — the map places every question at the country it is about, with counts per place (✓ happened · ✗ didn’t · ▢ awaiting · ◌ void); click a place to list its questions. Counts only — never a per-country accuracy score (far too few per place). Today it shows the July pilot’s skew: mostly the NATO summit in Ankara.

studiohow.text: Studio v3. One shell (map + slide card + time bar, OUR DATA in legend tokens vs THIS RUN in amber hatching), but each analysis type gets its own picture, because each looks in a different direction. SCENARIO looks FORWARD: branches off today to their dated triggers ◆; places drawn only if named AND in a source (Israel is not). COMPARE looks SIDEWAYS: Hormuz (A) vs US diesel (B) as two lanes, double rings on shared places, the judged A→B link. WHAT CHANGED looks BACK (new, replaces economic ripple, which is parked with economy): Iran's real risk readings as five lines (overall + 4 axes), gaps for no readings (23 Aug–3 Sep, and since 12 Sep), ● change-log entries you can click; BEFORE → AFTER bars; the change log with the event, the computed move (exact, ours) and the stored model explanation. Red dots/flags: 6 of the 14 explanations since 7 Jul fail a simple direction check (they explain a lower risk with something that got worse). FREE-FORM looks AT EVIDENCE: click a sentence and only its sources light up on the map and time bar (real Oman sources, 2–18 Aug). Stand-ins are labelled.

title.text: Global Perspectives — console redesign · approved designs (25 Sep 2026)

trhow.text: Track record (approved method). Stage buttons show how the top line changes: NOW = "We don’t have a scored track record yet"; FIRST MONTHS = the weekly locked sample, too few to judge; AFTER ~4 MONTHS = our score next to a base-rate guess, with the uncertainty. 1 · When we changed our read (real notes: France after the Normandy derailment, China after the Hong Kong vigil sentences; Germany honestly says no single event). 2 · This week’s settling — checking the pre-selected questions whose deadline passed, from the source named at publication, by a person who can’t see our probability. 3 · How a question looks on a story ([p] = its own probability, generated once the AI provider is back). 4 · July pilot archive, unscored. 5 · Counts that add up.

v2why.text: Two map modes (operator idea): GLOBE — spins on its own; touching or selecting stops it and turns the globe to face the story. RADAR 2D — a flat big board with a rotating radar beam; whatever the beam crosses lights up (pin flares, label appears) and its story is gently marked ◉ SCANNED in the feed — no auto-scroll, no focus theft. Stop/▶ control holds either motion; reduced-motion users get a still globe / beamless radar. Defaults: desktop opens on the spinning globe; phones and slow devices open on radar (cheap to draw). Also: XCOM-style HUD (brief · threat board · sensor status), honest Sensor status, Intel feed linked to pins, incoming-alert card. Continent dots here are placeholders — the real build uses GitHub-style dotted continents on the existing deck.gl globe.

v4board.text: Board WEB view redrawn (v4): the 14 most-linked stories from all 16 analyses merged — stories, not countries. X = peak date, rows = category, dot size = number of links, dashed line thickness = confidence (model judgment). Right: the same links as a list (the accessible version). Hover a dot for its StoryPeek. Clusters you can see: US–Iran → oil/diesel; Ukraine–Russia strikes → peace envoys; Israel–Palestine West Bank → settlement bans.

v4how.text: Try: (1) SHOW LINKED NEWS in the Timeline — 13 real headlines from 7 other stories appear at their own dates (4 inside this story’s span, 9 after it), tagged model-linked + confidence; never drawn as arrows from an event here. (2) Open other chapters; the ⚑ turning point (Aug 15) carries the “last 30 days analysed” caveat. (3) READ FULL on each cause step. (4) In Why it’s happening, each row leads with the cited dated headline, then the linked story, confidence per analysis (the diesel link: STRONG in US, Iran and Middle East analyses — never merged into one), the mechanism verbatim, and headlines cited from THIS story. (5) PREVIEW STATE shows the honest empty states. All content is live data from 25 Sep.

v5how.text: Story mode (operator: page too long → game-like). One screen, no scrolling. MAP (XCOM Geoscape frame) · SLIDES (Knight Lab StoryMap: each slide flies the map) · BOTTOM SCRUBBER (Flightradar24 / kepler.gl playback): news per day, 4 chapters, ⚑ Aug 15, linked-news ticks after Aug 21, TODAY, and forecast deadlines ◆ out to Dec 31 (XCOM dark-event countdown). Slides: BRIEF → CH1–CH4 (countries sized by real mention counts) → FED INTO (dashed arcs from Hormuz to the 7 linked stories; click a pin) → WATCH (triggers with days left). Left drawers WHY / WHO / VIEW FROM / SOURCES open over the map. READ IN FULL switches to the long page. Land dots are placeholders; places are approximate centroids.

nbhow.text: B · NOTEBOOK (Observable / Jupyter / NotebookLM). Reading-first and printable. Left: sources [1]–[4] (click for the verbatim snippet). Middle: cells — ASK → BOTTOM LINE → SCENARIO fork chart → WHERE (map; Israel not drawn) → WATCH table → CAUSE CHAIN (ours). + ADD CELL between cells runs another lens on the SAME sources (What changed chart, Compare grid, Free-form) — several analyses stacked in one document. Hover a citation → its source lights in the rail. Right: CHECKS + SHARE / COPY / PRINT. Strength: depth + multiple lenses. Weakness: least visual, scrolls.

boardhow.text: C · CASE BOARD (Obra Dinn / detective corkboard / Disco Elysium). One run laid out spatially: EVIDENCE cards [1]–[4] → REASONING (bottom line + claims, hatched = this run; the stored cause chain in green = ours) → OUTCOMES (60/20/20 scenario cards with dated ◆ triggers). Strings: 'supports' solid cyan; claim→scenario amber dotted (model judgment); a red TENSION between [1] (US: blockade indefinitely) and [4] (Iran: end the war from strength). Click a card: its strings light, the rest dims; drawer shows connections. FAILED CHECKS turns bad claims red. Strength: shows the reasoning, most game-like. Weakness: dense; one run only (saved cases stay parked).

chathow.text: D · CONVERSATION + LIVE CANVAS (Claude artifacts / Perplexity / ChatGPT canvas). Left: a thread of 3 turns on the same stories — Scenario → Free-form (Oman, adds sources [5]–[8]) → What changed (Iran log). Each answer: type tag, amber THIS RUN label, SHOW ON CANVAS. Right: the canvas switches to the active turn's picture (fork bands / evidence map + source timeline / risk chart with flagged ● marks). Composer with lens chips + suggested follow-ups; each follow-up is a new run on the reader's key. SHARE THREAD freezes all turns. Strength: most familiar, natural follow-ups. Weakness: closest to a generic chatbot; cost grows per turn.

studiopay.text: Whichever direction wins, add the reader-pays pieces (runs use the reader's own key): BEFORE the run — what is sent (stories, ~tokens), provider + model + output cap, deep research on/off, per-story material RICH / THIN (only 17 stories are rich today — warn before they spend). AFTER — a receipt from the provider's usage field (tokens in/out, model, time), checks, shareable or not; if checks fail: 'your provider still charged for this run'. Money shown only from a verified dated price table (operator decision), else link to the provider's pricing.

gTitle.text: G · Site navigation (N1 approved) + phone pattern (P1 proposed)

navhow.text: Navigation after a 3-way debate (five doors / game HUD / by job) + 2 critics. MENU: Map · Stories · Briefings · Studio · Track record — plain words, no dropdowns ('Console', 'Topics', 'Threads' were jargon). Countries = a map layer + a tab in Stories, not a menu item (~90 requests in 30 days). Account at right; the parked credits badge stays hidden. STATUS LINE under the menu: 'New stories and analysis paused since 12 Sep' — 12 Sep verified (last daily brief 12 Sep 14:01 UTC); computed from the newest data, not typed, so it clears itself. PHONE: bottom tab bar with the same 5 items. URLS: new labels, same URLs — our hosting can't send real 301s and story links are built in 8 places outside the site (emails, RSS, LinkedIn, alerts). Only one new route: /briefings. Maps live inside each page (no always-on map under every page: battery/memory cost on reading pages). SEARCH: later — no search index exists yet.

phonehow.text: Phone pattern after a 3-way debate (map + bottom sheet / swipe cards / read first) + a critic: a hybrid of READ-FIRST + the BOTTOM SHEET. Every page: header + 'paused since 12 Sep' line, ONE tab switch, content, 5-item tab bar. Default tab is READ (the slides as one scroll) — except the Map page, which opens on the radar map. MAP is a tab: the WebGL map loads only then (the map is already lazy-loaded per route today), and the slide card becomes a bottom sheet (peek / half / full, handle + buttons). TIMELINE (or EDITIONS / LOG) is the third tab. Track record swaps READ for BOARD. Studio's READ puts the QUOTE first (here: all 4 stories are THIN — a real warning) and the RECEIPT last; the board view is off on phones. Rejected: swipe cards (a small map per card can't show compare lanes / fork bands; re-rendering the map per card), static map thumbnails (go stale). Pick a page at the top; try PEEK / HALF / FULL on the MAP phone.
